fieldMarks: Very large jackrabbit with especially large head and tall ears (average 162 mm), mostly bare apart from white fringes on edges and tips.
Flanks, limbs, hips and rump white with black tips; belly, chin, throat and tail white.
Upper body yellow-brown with some black.
behavior: Primarily nocturnal and crepuscular, also active in the morning; rests in shade by day in forms under grass, brush, cactus or mesquite.
May travel up to about a mile between daytime cover and nocturnal feeding area; fast runner with great leaping ability.
Eats grasses, mesquite, cacti and other desert plants; relies on mesquite leaves and cacti in the dry season and grass in the wet season.
NatureServe says it may form groups up to 25; Animal Diversity Web calls it solitary.
habitat: Arid grassy areas with scattered large shrubs, desert with little grass, foothills, mesas and bajadas; less common in barren desert and valley-bottom mesquite.
range: Southern Arizona through western Mexico to northern Nayarit, and Tiburon Island; sea level to about 1,500 m in Arizona.
